messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - Hosted API 503 spike in us-west-2 inference cluster. Error rate 503s ~12% over last 3m, tail latency > 5s for token generation. Impact: multiple hosted API customers (region us-west-2). Paging oncall @alex and SRE rotation. Links: https://observability.internal/rum/cluster/us-west-2 — please ACK and start mitigation.

alex: ACK. I'm oncall and looking at the autoscaler and LB health. Initial hypothesis: noisy NICs on a subset of instances or upstream network flapping. I'll gather pod/node mappings.

marta: adding @aws-support to thread — we saw similar patterns earlier when ENIs were reassigned. @aws-support can you confirm if there were any networking control-plane events in us-west-2 starting ~1979002000?

aws-support: Hi team — AWS Eng here. We're investigating a networking control-plane event in us-west-2 that started ~35m ago affecting a subset of instances in az-2. We're pulling VPC flow logs and checking for ENI failovers. We'll update in 10m. If you can provide specific instance IDs/ENI ids we can correlate faster.

samir: grabbing instance IDs now from the runtime dashboard. Pushing a filtered query -> found high retry counts on instances: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b, i-0b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c. Also seeing elevated kube restarts on inference-worker pods. Starting a rolling reroute to healthy pool with model-variant fallback to quantized-variant-1 for low-latency customers.

alex: good. Begun reroute policy: route 50% traffic away from affected nodes to dedicated spare pool; 50% to canary quantized-variant-1. This should reduce errors while we wait on upstream. I'll also bump request timeouts for clients in that pool to avoid cascading retries.

julia: heads-up for CS: customers complaining about 503s. Drafting a short proactive notification. Will post to status page after confirmation from ops.

samir: Draft status page update (draft):
```
Summary: We are investigating increased errors and latency for the Hosted API in us-west-2. Impact: a subset of customers in the region may see 503s or higher latency. Current status: Mitigation in progress — traffic is being rerouted to healthy pools and canary model variants to restore service.
Estimated scope: Partial region impact; not every customer.
{what we're doing}: Working with cloud provider to identify and remediate network control-plane issues; performing targeted reroutes and instance remediation.
Next update: in 15 minutes or upon significant change.
```

marta: Looks good. Suggest adding "Affected features: text generation, streaming responses" and include the incident id: INC-1979002345. Also remove technical detail in the public status page about ENIs; keep that for internal comms and vendor updates.

alex: Agreed. I'll publish the status page now (brief) and then we can escalate with AWS for host replacements if the control-plane doesn't stabilize.

statusbot: Status page updated: incident INC-1979002345 — https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-1979002345 :eyes: :loud_sound:

julia: Customer notification draft for emails (short):
```
Subject: Service interruption in us-west-2 — brief update
Body: We're aware of elevated errors and latency affecting the Hosted API in us-west-2. Our engineering teams are working to mitigate impact by routing traffic to healthy capacity. We will provide updates on our status page. If you see ongoing issues after 30 minutes, please reply and we'll prioritize.
```

ops_manager: +1 on that. Keep tone concise, avoid internal jargon. For customers on Dedicated plans, add a note about private channel and ETA for remediation once AWS confirms.

alex: AWS update: they see ENI churn and a subset of instances where the hypervisor is reattaching ENIs — they're recommending replacement of the affected instances. They've asked for permission to perform host replacements for the listed instance IDs. We should approve.

marta: Approve host replacement for the two affected instances. But plan for the host replacement to take ~8-12 minutes; maintain reroutes and notify customers when replacements complete. Who will coordinate the replacement window with AWS? @alex?

alex: I'll coordinate with AWS. @aws-support please proceed with host replacement for i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b and i-0b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c. Please perform one at a time and confirm when each is done so we can validate traffic.

aws-support: Roger. Starting replacement of i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b now. We'll post updates here.

samir: While replacements are happening, I'm increasing cache TTL on common prefixes to reduce load on the inference layer and lowering batch sizes for the spare pool to stabilize latency.

alex: Note for on-call handoff: I'm due to hand off to @marta in ~25 minutes. If AWS confirms the first host replacement completes cleanly, I'll do the handoff with a summary. Otherwise I'll extend and stay.

aws-support: Replacement complete for i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b. Observability shows error rate down to 6% from 12% in the affected pool. Proceeding with replacement of i-0b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c.

julia: Posting customer update now (email + status page): "We've implemented mitigations and are seeing early improvement; full remediation in progress." Sending to impacted customer list.

samir: After second replacement completes, we should run a small regression eval against canary traffic to ensure output fidelity for quantized-variant-1. Also schedule a follow-up retrospective template for post-incident notes.

ops_manager: Good call. Please capture the timeline, decisions (reroute, host replacement, TTL bump), and customer comms in the postmortem doc. Flag any follow-ups to PMs and security if keys or audit logs needed.

aws-support: Replacement of i-0b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c complete. Metrics show stable ENI attachment and error rate down to ~1-2% across the region; we'll continue to monitor for another 30 minutes.

alex: Seeing stabilization on metrics and customer reports. I'll proceed with the on-call handoff to @marta now. Handoff note: mitigation actions taken — 1) 50% reroute to spare pool; 2) 50% to quantized-variant-1 canary; 3) approved host replacements and AWS performed sequential replacements; 4) cache TTL bumped and batch sizes tuned. Current state: healthy, monitoring. If regressions appear, wake me.

marta: Taking handoff. I'll keep watch for 30 more minutes and verify the fidelity eval when samir posts results. Thanks @alex for driving the first wave.

samir: Running the regression eval now — small sample looks OK, perplexity in expected range. I'll attach results to the postmortem doc and close the incident when metrics remain low for 30m.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1979002345 status changed to RESOLVED (monitoring). Start time: 1979002345. Resolution summary: Host replacements by AWS and traffic reroutes reduced 503s and latency. Follow-up: postmortem + vendor RCA request to AWS.

julia: Customer final notification drafted and queued: "Service restored; we're monitoring. A post-incident update with root cause and mitigations will follow." Sending now.

ops_manager: Nice work team. Please remember to request the formal RCA from AWS and add it to the vendor communications folder. Also schedule the postmortem meeting tomorrow EOD for stakeholders.

marta: Created postmortem stub and assigned owners for timeline (alex), vendor RCA (ops_manager), and customer comms follow-up (julia). Closing this thread but leaving links in the incident tracker.

statusbot: Incident INC-1979002345 — RESOLVED. https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-1979002345 :white_check_mark:
